about: Branch's rename map (DECISIONS.md item 127). Read by scripts/rebrand.mjs. Every word is matched case-insensitively, also inside longer names (OpenClawConfig, OPENCLAW_HOME, skillCurator), and replaced in the matched text's case: all capitals, a leading capital, or lower case. Before the words, each phrase rule renames the product name where it stands as a word in text (DECISIONS.md item 133: "Branch Agent"). Protected spans and skipped files are never changed. docs/foundation/REBRAND.md explains every entry.

the local clone of the upstream
references to the upstream's own issues and pull requests (openclaw#123)
links to real outside sites (upstream docs, GitHub, npm, image registry): renaming them would break the link
the same outside sites written without a scheme
GitHub, image-registry and repo names of the upstream project
npm packages published by the upstream that the engine installs from the registry (also as pnpm writes them in file names): their names cannot change
names exported or read by those outside packages (fs-safe, crabline, tokenjuice), and their own subpaths such as tokenjuice/openclaw
the upstream's native app kit (apps/ is not part of Branch); one data file of it is kept at its upstream path
copyright and licence notices stay as the upstream wrote them (MIT)
the notice file name that the upstream's patch adds to a third-party package (patches/ is skipped)
an option name of the outside package @openclaw/crabline, used where the engine calls it
the outside package @clawdbot/lobster, its import path, its workflow file extension and the variables it reads (only the bare .lobster extension; CSS classes such as .lobster-pet are renamed)
legacy names kept in code only so old configs still load (item 135)
the outside npm package clawpdf (the PDF library): its name cannot change

skip.why: the MIT licence and third-party notices stay unchanged
Branch's own notes, already in Branch's words and citing the upstream pin
the upstream's release history: it records what OpenClaw shipped, with its contributors' names
the upstream's release feeds (its macOS app's release notes)
patches to third-party packages: their bytes are hash-locked in the lockfile and patches/README.md, and their notices record the upstream's own changes
the rename tools and their record
